title: Queens of the Stone Age Announce Epic 2027 U.S. Tour Dates – Full Pitchfork Reveal
body:
The legendary rock outfit Queens of the Stone Age have unveiled a sprawling U.S. tour slated for the spring of 2027, marking the band’s first major American circuit in more than a decade. The itinerary launches with a four‑city California sweep in May, featuring opening acts the iconic Pixies and the up‑and‑coming Wheelchair Sports Camp. The announcement arrives on the heels of the band’s recent television debut of their new single “Where the Goth Girls At?” on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, signaling a renewed push into mainstream visibility.

The tour’s structure reflects a strategic blend of nostalgia and forward momentum. By pairing themselves with the Pixies—a band whose influence on alternative rock is as profound as QOTSA’s own—Queens of the Stone Age tap into a shared fanbase that spans three generations. The inclusion of Wheelchair Sports Camp, a rising act known for their genre‑bending blend of post‑punk and experimental rock, adds a fresh edge to the bill and underscores QOTSA’s commitment to supporting emerging talent. Industry analysts note that such lineups can boost ticket sales across demographics, offering seasoned fans the comfort of familiar sounds while introducing younger audiences to the band’s evolving catalogue.

The timing of the tour is noteworthy. After a period of relative quiet punctuated by sporadic festival appearances and a handful of studio releases, the band appears poised to re‑establish a consistent live presence. Their recent performance on Fallon, where they premiered “Where the Goth Girls At?”—a track that melds Homme’s signature desert‑rock riffs with darker, synth‑laden textures—has already generated buzz on streaming platforms, climbing into the top ten of several alternative charts. Critics have praised the song for its lyrical wit and sonic daring, suggesting it could become a set‑list staple that bridges the band’s early desert‑rock era with their more experimental recent work.

From a logistical standpoint, the tour’s routing demonstrates a careful balance between market demand and operational efficiency. Beginning with four California dates—Los Angeles, San Diego, San Francisco, and Sacramento—allows the band to capitalize on the state’s dense population of rock enthusiasts while minimizing early‑tour travel fatigue. Subsequent legs will likely sweep the Southwest, the Midwest, and the East Coast, though details remain under wraps. Ticket vendors have reported an immediate sell‑through of the initial California shows, prompting speculation that additional dates could be added in response to demand, a pattern the band has followed in past tours.

The announcement also arrives amid a broader resurgence of legacy rock acts touring extensively after the pandemic’s disruption of live music. Queens of the Stone Age’s decision to embark on a full‑scale U.S. run signals confidence in the market’s recovery and in the band’s enduring relevance. Their ability to draw sizable crowds without relying on nostalgia alone—evidenced by the fresh material being showcased—suggests a sustainable model for veteran groups seeking to remain culturally and commercially vital.

Looking ahead, the 2027 tour could serve as a catalyst for further creative output from the band. Historically, extensive touring cycles have coincided with periods of prolific songwriting for QOTSA, often culminating in surprise releases or deluxe reissues. Fans and critics alike will be watching to see whether the momentum generated by the new single and the high‑profile tour will translate into additional studio work or collaborative projects. Regardless of the outcome, Queens of the Stone Age’s return to the road reaffirms their status as a cornerstone of modern rock, poised to shape the genre’s landscape for years to come.
